title: A cat called Pilot

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

chapters.title: The cat under the car

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is animals and pets. And Leyla has news.
[laugh] I do! I'm going to let the cat out of the bag — literally. I have a cat now.
No way! Since when?
Since last Tuesday. It was raining, and I heard a little sound under a car. It was a tiny stray kitten, wet and very scared.
Oh, poor thing. So you took him home?
Not at first. I wanted to adopt him immediately, but my mum said, "Hold your horses. First take him to the vet."
Smart mum.
So the next morning I took him to a veterinarian. He was healthy, just hungry. Now he lives with me. His name is Pilot.
Pilot?
Because he jumps from the wardrobe to the sofa like a plane. [chuckle]
I love it. I grew up with dogs. Dogs are so easy to love — they're domesticated, they want to be your friend.
Cats are different. They're tame, but they decide when they want to be your friend.
True. So, can I say something? The elephant in the room is that I'm a bit scared of cats.
[laugh] Sam! Pilot weighs one kilo!
I know! But in the wild, cats are predators. I respect them.
Speaking of the wild — last week I read about the snow leopard. It lives in the mountains, even in the Caucasus, and it is endangered.
Why is it endangered?
People are taking its habitat for farms and roads, and some still hunt it. There are only a few thousand left in the world.
That's terrible. I hope people protect them.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: do you have a pet — or which animal would you like to have, and why?
Not a cat. Sorry, Pilot. See you next time!
Bye for now!
